title: restoreFromBackup's crash-recovery flow has no account-changed guard before re-arming mirroring

text: Discovered while implementing plan-3a (S3). MigrationCoordinator.restoreFromBackup (the raw-SQLite migration-crash-recovery restore, Sync/MigrationCoordinator.swift ~line 203-253) calls host.attachStore(at: prev) to reattach at the pre-crash previousMode with no accountStateProvider check anywhere in the method — unlike runMigration's four ops, which all now refuse when the signed-in account changed out from under them (S3's fix). Narrow compound scenario: a migration crashes mid-flight, then before the user triggers restoreFromBackup's recovery, the device's iCloud account changes; if previousMode == .iCloudSync, the restore reattaches with mirroring armed against the NEW account while restoring the pre-crash local backup — a live variant of the exact bug S3 exists to fix, just on the crash-recovery path rather than the primary migration path. Flagged for consideration by the wave-2b closing report ('consider whether it needs one before 3a lands its own probe elsewhere'); not fixed in 3a to keep scope bounded to the plan's four named findings (S3 S13 S21 S24) — filed per the LIL-77 discovered-residual precedent instead of silently expanding scope on an already-large plan. Fix shape: add the same accountStateProvider-consulted-before-attachStore guard runMigration's ops already have, placed after tearDownStore (recovery-anchor already captured) but before host.attachStore(at: prev) when prev == .iCloudSync.
